items.title: Cont. of a Study to Evaluate Implanting Peripheral Nerve Grafts Into Subjects With Parkinson's Disease (PD) During DBS
items.summary: This pilot study is designed to follow up on a previous, preliminary study and test the long-term safety and feasibility of the implantation of autologous peripheral nerve grafts into the substantia nigra, basal forebrain, putamen, and/or STN of participants with PD undergoing deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery. Peripheral nerve tissue contains Schwann cells which produce growth factors that have been demonstrated to support the survival and function of neurons. Participants will serve as their own donor for the tissue, which will be implanted at the time they undergo DBS surgery.

items.summary: We thank the authors (Weide et al. 1 ) for their evaluation of our algorithm, which predicts optimal deep-brain stimulation contact points in Parkinson's disease. Their analysis on an independent dataset highlights practical challenges of translating predictive tools into routine clinical use. Here, we clarify key methodological points, discuss the robustness of the algorithm, and emphasize the need for broader validation across diverse clinical centers to fully demonstrate its utility.
